title: Dong Nguyen pulled Flappy Bird himself.
description:
Dong Nguyen pulled Flappy Bird himself. In his first interview after removing the game, Nguyen told Forbes he had received no legal threat from Nintendo over the pipe graphics, and that any resemblance was 'coincidental'.

He walked away from it anyway. Nguyen would not confirm the exact figure to Forbes, saying only: 'I don't know the exact figure, but I do know it's a lot.'

Removed his own number one app from every app store that February, saying it had become 'an addictive product' and that he 'couldn't sleep'.

and called them 'harmless'. Nguyen said he would pull Super Ball Juggling and Shuriken Block too, the moment he thought players were getting addicted to those as well.

He coded the whole game in two or three days, the year before. Explaining why he killed it took a slow forty-five minute interview, through a haze of cigarette smoke.

Sources:
- https://www.forbes.com/sites/lananhnguyen/2014/02/11/exclusive-flappy-bird-creator-dong-nguyen-says-app-gone-forever-because-it-was-an-addictive-product: Forbes' exclusive interview with Dong Nguyen, conducted in a Hanoi hotel on condition his face not be shown, his first since removing the game. Source for the direct quotes, the denial of any Nintendo legal threat, the two other apps he kept live, his stated reason for pulling the game, the 24 May 2013 release date, and the two or three days he says it took him to code it.
